summary.headline: Subex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.7% YoY to INR 79.45 crore, with EBITDA margin at 21.2% and management signalling margins will be held in a range.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 8.9% QoQ and 19.7% YoY to INR 79.45 crore, with EBITDA of INR 16.87 crore (21.2% margin) versus INR 10.58 crore in Q4. Normalized PAT was INR 16.09 crore versus INR 11.51 crore previously, and reported PAT was INR 14.22 crore. Management framed FY27 as a growth year, while saying it will hold margins in a range and reinvest excess cash in R&D and AI. Cash stood at INR 184.8 crore, and management declined to give a funnel number, order-book value or a revenue target, citing competitive sensitivity.

segments.name: Partner Ecosystem Management (PEM / wholesale billing)
segments.commentary: Management called it an under-invested business that has been rebuilt; it renewed a Tier 1 Asia-Pacific PEM engagement this quarter and sees stronger deal flow. No quantified revenue was given.

segments.name: RAFM (Revenue Assurance and Fraud Management)
segments.commentary: Secured new business assurance and fraud management deal with a leading European operator; a FraudZap customer deal was said to be slipping into this quarter. Management said FraudZap's investment is already recovered, though no margin figure was given.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance. Management said it will not give forward guidance on the call; expects 'double-digit' or 'high single digit' growth, to be decided.
Margins to be held 'in the ballpark' of the FY26 close and the mid-to-high teens was not confirmed; management will hold margins in a range and reinvest excess cash in R&D/AI.
R&D intensity to rise; target horizon split of 60/30/10 (H1/H2/H3) over the next two years.
Management aims to reach INR 100 crore quarterly top line in 'a few quarters' with backlog-driven visibility; no date committed.
Board is considering capital restructuring (reducing equity against losses) via a consultant, with board, shareholder and NCLT approvals needed; long process.
ESOP: 5% approved; up to 2% to be acquired from market in FY27, with execution expected around Q3 after postal ballot.
capex_capacity: R&D headcount about 700 in total, with about 200 in core R&D teams.
Middle East delivery offshored to Bangalore; on-site resources in Dubai, Kuwait and Qatar pulled back.
Implementation cycle from contract to subscription revenue is 4-5 quarters; internal goal to cut by one quarter, with recent project closed about 45 days early.
Possible acquisition: management said cash can be used for inorganic options; it is on the radar but no active talks.
Q2 FY27 fair value markup planned for the stake in an unlisted company received on sale of ID Central.
demand_pricing: Qualified pipeline stated at 3-4x the annual order-intake target; management said 70% of revenue is recurring and 30% is won in-year.
Middle East: slowdown in orders and deal timing, not cancellations; a Tier 1 Middle East renewal was secured.
US described as better; Europe described as okay; APAC and Africa described as slower; contracts slipping by a month or two.
Deals above USD 0.8-1 million go through RFP; management would not disclose margin thresholds for contract acceptance.
Management said FY26 announced deals were about INR 18-20 million (unclear units; transcript says 'in the range of five' then '18-20 million').

qa_highlights.question: Has the board considered reducing equity capital against accumulated losses?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said it was discussed at the board meeting held the day before; a consultant will be appointed, and it is a long process requiring board, shareholder and NCLT approval.

qa_highlights.question: Size of executable pipeline and total order wins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave qualified pipeline at 3-4x target but declined to give absolute numbers, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Where will EBITDA margins stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins expected 'in the ballpark' of current levels; management will not cap margins but will reinvest excess cash in R&D and AI.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East exposure and sectoral contract recoveries?
qa_highlights.answer: Sectoral contract litigation continues: one of three entities settled, two others being chased for closure this quarter; the remaining one is in Middle East courts with no firm timeline. Middle East subsidiary is self-sufficient, with no further capital infusion expected.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue increase was FX?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO estimated about INR 3 crore of currency gain in the quarter; QoQ FX gain was small.

qa_highlights.question: Acquisition and ESOP timing?
qa_highlights.answer: ESOP: postal ballot planned within about two weeks; purchases expected around Q3 for up to 2% in FY27. Inorganic options under review, but no active talks.

risks_watch: Middle East slowdown and volatility: order deferrals, litigation outside India, and offshoring of delivery.
Deal timing slippage (1-2 months) from legal and liability negotiations; management said nothing lost yet.
Margin reinvestment: management signalled R&D/AI spend will rise, which may pressure the 21.2% margin.
Revenue growth remains unquantified; investors pressed for explicit guidance and management declined.
Equity restructuring and ESOP share purchases are pending approvals; the timing is uncertain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and turnaround, but evasive on pipeline, order value, margin thresholds and growth targets, citing competitive sensitivity. Cautious on Middle East and APAC deal timing, and on near-term margin expansion.
key_quotes: Revenue for the quarter grew 8.9% sequentially and 19.7% over the corresponding quarter last year.
Nothing is lost, though. We haven't, like, lost any big deal and all that right now.
I have a line of sight. I could not have said that.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.7% YoY to INR 79.45 crore and management calls FY27 a growth year with a qualified pipeline at 3-4x the order-intake target, but no numeric revenue guidance was given (double-digit vs high single digit still undecided) and no physical capacity additions or utilisation were disclosed.
